title: Shadow of the Gun: Iraqi Militias Vow to Keep Arms as U.S. Forces Prepare Exit
snippet: With the final U.S. troops preparing to depart Iraq, local armed factions are signaling that their arsenals will remain fully intact, posing a major challenge for Baghdad's future stability.
content:
WASHINGTON — As the final contingent of U.S. military personnel prepares to pack up and leave Iraq, a daunting challenge hangs over the nation's fragile stability. Local and regional militia groups are sending an unmistakable message to both Baghdad and Washington: their weapons are here to stay.

A Lingering Power Vacuum

The U.S. military drawdown represents the closing chapter of a multi-decade American engagement in the region. However, security experts warn that the departure creates a precarious environment. Over the past decade, various armed factions—many backed by Iran—have entrenched themselves deep within Iraq's political and military infrastructure, operating with near impunity.

Defiance in Baghdad

Despite calls from government officials and international observers for non-state actors to disarm and integrate into national security forces, militia commanders remain defiant. They argue that their arsenals are vital for national defense and regional deterrence, signaling that no official troop withdrawal will compel them to lay down their arms.
